newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Sterling eyes 2.85 marks in Europe.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Sterling eyes 2.85 marks in Europe.

text.p: Sterling, hovering just below 57-month peaks at 2.8440 marks, has not exhausted its upside potential and is now targeting 2.85-marks resistance.
Sterling/mark re-visited 57-month peaks on Monday after setting them on Friday, and analysts said its upside momentum is not exhausted yet.

"The target is 2.8660/2.8700, with interim resistance at 2.85 marks," said Francoise Skelley, head of global trading technical analysis at Credit Suisse First Boston. Skelley said a push towards 2.85 was likely on Monday, with gains beyond expected later in the week.
"On the daily charts, it (sterling/mark) is not overbought at all. The nine-day RSI is around 63 percent, that is not very high at all," said CS First Boston's Skelley.
The 14-day RSI was at 60 percent on Monday.
AT 0845 GMT, sterling/mark was trading at 2.8365/75 against 2.8440/50 in late Europe on Friday.
On a sterling move lower, Skelley said support around 2.8330/2.8250 marks should be activated.
Cable is expected to ease a touch on Monday.
"Overall, I expect it will drift down to $1.6220/05...But it is very stuck and particularly neutral," said Skelley.
At 0810 GMT, cable stood at $1.6360/71 against $1.6371/76 in late Europe on Friday.
Chartists said while cable was likely to drift lower, it was lacking the momentum needed to break out of well-worn ranges around $1.64 and $1.6250.
Sterling/dollar faces resistance at $1.6400/15 and very short-term support at $1.6330 on the hourly charts.
"But it is fairly stuck," said CS First Boston's Skelley.
Analysts have also said cable needs to break above $1.64 and $1.6432 to attempt a convincing push higher.
RSI - 14 day: Stg/mark: 61 pct, Stg/dollar: 51 pct
